chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Nawfalī, who said:

Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj said to me that Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام wrote to him: “O Muḥammad, put your affairs together and take your precaution.” He said: “So I was putting my affairs together, and I did not know what he had written to me, until a messenger came to me, carried me away from Miṣr in fetters, seized everything I owned, and I remained in prison for eight years.”

Then a letter came to me from him in the prison, in which was: “O Muḥammad, do not reside in the district of the western side.” So I read the letter and said: “He writes this to me while I am in prison? Indeed, this is astonishing.” Then it was not long before I was released, and all praise is due to Allah.

He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj wrote to him asking him about his estates, so he wrote to him: “They will soon be returned to you, and what harm is there to you if they are not returned to you?” Then when Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj went to al-ʿAskar, an order was written for the return of his estates, but he died before that.

He said: Aḥmad ibn al-Khaḍīb wrote to Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj asking him about going out to al-ʿAskar. So he wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام seeking his counsel, and he wrote to him: “Go out, for in it will be your relief, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.” So he went out, and he did not remain long except a little while until he died.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam عليه السلام referred to in the report
key_terms.أَجْمِعْ أَمْرَكَ: Put your affairs in order and prepare carefully
key_terms.خُذْ حِذْرَكَ: Take precaution and be on guard

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the guidance of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام to Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj during imprisonment and hardship?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates reports concerning Muḥammad ibn al-Faraj and the correspondence of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, including warnings, foreknowledge of imprisonment and release, and mention of his estates and eventual death. It reflects the Imam’s guidance during times of hardship and political pressure, and records events connected to al-ʿAskar and those associated with him.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Al Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Nowfaly who said,

‘Muhammad Bin Al-Faraj said to me that Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (10<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) wrote to him: ‘O Muhammad! Gather your affairs and take your caution’. He said, ‘So I was gathering my affairs and I didn’t know what he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to me (its meaning) until a messenger came over to me and carried me away from Egypt, and struck upon (confiscated) everything that I owned, and I was in prison for eight years.

Then a letter arrived to me from him<sup>asws</sup> in prison in which he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘O Muhammad! Do not lodge in the western side’. So I wrote the letter and I said (to myself), ‘He<sup>asws</sup> write to me with this and I am in prison. This is strange!’. So it wasn’t long before they released me, and the Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And Muhammad Bin Al-Faraj wrote to him<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about his estate. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘Soon they would be returned to you, and it would not harm you if there are not returned to you’. When Muhammad Bin Al-Faraj went to Al-Askar, it was written to him for the return of his estate, and he died before that’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And Ahmad Bin Al-Khazeyb wrote to Muhammad Bin Al-Faraj asking him of the going out to Al-Askar. So he wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> consulting him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘Go out, for therein is your relief, if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted so Desires’. So he went out, and he did not remain except for a little until he died’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali who has said the following.

“Muhammad ibn al-Faraj told me that abu al-Hassan (a.s.) has written to him this. “O Muhammad, organize you affairs and be careful.” He said that he began to organize his affairs and did not know what the Imam (a.s.) meant thereby until police came to me and took me out of Egypt as a captive. All of my belongings were confiscated and I remained in prison for eight years.

In the prison I received a letter from him that said, “O Muhammad, do not reside in the western location.” I read the letter and said to my self, “He writes me this and I am in prison. This is strange.” Shortly afterwards, I was released, thanks to Allah.

The narrator has said that Muhammad ibn al-Faraj wrote to him about his properties. The Imam (a.s.) wrote to him in response, “Your properties will soon be returned to you and even if they are not returned to you it will not harm you.” When Muhammad al-Faraj left to the army camp (Samarra) an order was issued to release his properties but he died before receiving them.

The narrator has said that Ahmad ibn al-Khadib wrote to Muhammad ibn al-Faraj asking him to come to the army camp. He wrote to the Imam (a.s.) for his advise in the matter and the response was this. “ Go out. In it there will be happiness and relief for you, by the will of Allah, the Most High..” He left for the journey but very shortly afterwards he died.”
